purpose: Direct visual-reference redesign using August 2014 UE4 screenshots after flat modern revisions rejected
reference_mode: last three images: Persona crop, UMG crop, actual Quader editor
prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create ONE new full Quader level-editor UI mockup. The user wants the actual MOOD OF EARLY UNREAL ENGINE 4 circa 2014. Use the PROVIDED REAL 2014 SCREENSHOTS as the style source, not a generic interpretation of "professional dark UI".

REFERENCE ROLES IN ORDER:
Image 1: genuine UE4 4.4 Persona editor from August 2014. PRIMARY STYLE SOURCE: study the sculpted tabs, medium-gray toolbar deck, recessed content, pictorial shaded icons, lighter inset controls, different control families and strong layer seams.
Image 2: genuine UE4 4.4 UMG editor from August 2014. SECOND STYLE SOURCE: study its compact uneven composition, beveled pane structure, small text, rich multi-value gray palette, icon toolbar and warm orange active tab. Use CHROME ONLY, not its central game menu, timeline, animation tools, text, logo or functionality.
Image 3: real Quader editor. This is FUNCTIONAL CONTENT ONLY, not a style reference. Recompose and redraw the UI while retaining Quader's actual menus, modeling tools, Outliner, viewport, Inspector, Face Texture, Layers and Asset Browser. No Unreal branding or copied literal icons; create Quader-owned icons in the same pictorial tradition.

THE CRITICAL CORRECTION:
Earlier attempts failed because they were too flat, too homogenized, too perfectly arranged like a contemporary design-system showcase, with black slabs and tidy tiny purple highlights. DO NOT repeat that look. NO flat SaaS grid, no identical squared control treatment, no modern minimal "premium" finish. This should feel like substantial, opinionated working software from the early UE4 period, with visual depth and the character of a collection of specialized tools. All UI surfaces remain dark or medium charcoal; no light-theme backgrounds.

WHAT TO TAKE DIRECTLY FROM THE REAL STYLE REFERENCES:
- Medium gray structural decks and window rails, dark-gray panels, charcoal recesses: the full usable gray range, not everything almost black. Think #565656 toolbar, #404040 working panes, #292929 recesses, #171717 narrow seams. Slightly warm grays.
- Visibly shaped controls. Beveled dock TAB HEADS protrude into their rails, with subtle slopes and small close buttons, not full-width flat title ribbons everywhere. Fitted viewport framing with a shallow double edge. Raised pictorial command buttons, rounded inset dropdowns, narrow spin fields and different tree/thumb/list surfaces. Short old-school gradients and bevel highlights are REQUIRED here; they must be obvious enough to feel sculpted. They should look functional and modest, not chrome, glass, a spaceship or a gaming overlay.
- Pictorial, shaded native tool icons. Tools should feel individually illustrated, with distinctive silhouettes, small specular highlights, shadows and blue/steel/ochre/copper color details. A cube/extrude tool can depict a shaded block with one orange face; knife a small steel blade; mirror two split volumes; arrays repeated little blocks. Avoid a row of identical generic cube icons or delicate line symbols.
- Varied tool rhythm. A few larger icon-over-label commands, beside very compact dropdown clusters and thin separators. Hierarchy should follow tool function. Not every button or pane needs the same width, height or corner radius. The overall layout is coherent and usable but not mechanically regular or overdesigned.
- Warm orange/ochre active states like early UE4: one strong active scene/dock tab and selected Outliner row, localized and functional. The Quader Q logo stays purple but do not tint the whole app purple. Red/green/blue axis labels and authored multicolored tool symbols give functional color variety.

QUADER CONTENT AND WORKING COMPOSITION:
A wide desktop screen, a modest Quader Q logo in a dark sculpted native title rail, title "Quader — Hallway.qdr".
Menus: "File  Edit  View  Select  Create  Object  Mesh  Vertex  Edge  Face  UV  Window  Help".
Below: an old-style toolbar deck with the actual "Object Mode", "Groups", "Grid: 32", "Angle: 15°", "Texture Lock", "Texture Lock Scale" controls. Give the mode/group symbols real icon character and substantial relief.
Left: the existing modeling tool rail, with small shaded icons and labels Pivot, Extrude, Insert Edge Loop, Knife, Cut, Mirror, Poly, Linear Array, Radial Array, Path Array, UV Peel. Place beside an Outliner with compact nested rows: Hallway, Floor, Walls, North wall, East wall, Columns, Column 01, Column 02, Column 03, Stairs. Do not stretch rows into tall evenly spaced cards. Selected Walls row warm ochre. Dock title is a shaped tab over a medium-gray frame.
Center: ONE generous Perspective viewport, with scene tab "Hallway". Compact native strip of move/rotate/scale/snapping controls plus "Environment", "Perspective", "Shaded". Show simple graybox architecture: a floor, two perpendicular tall walls, several plain square pillars and stairs, viewed obliquely from above on a grid. Gray shaded geometry, selected wall outlined warm yellow/orange, ordinary RGB transform gizmo. It is a real blockout level, no cinematic scene, no game menu, no character. The viewport remains the largest single region. Its UI framing should resemble the weight and depth of the reference, with no giant margins.
Right: dense Inspector dock with small recognizable tab/close glyphs, compact collapsible bars General, Transform, Export, Lighting. Name Walls, Hidden and Locked checkboxes. Transform has distinct Position/Rotation/Scale groups, each with vertically STACKED X/Y/Z values; editable fields visibly inset with readable medium-gray faces, small arrow gutters, minimal spacing. Show Face Texture and Layers as smaller retained sections below. Use no isolated rounded property cards.
Bottom: Asset Browser with shaped dock tab, compact Search assets / All assets / view icons toolbar. Project folder tree Materials / Scenes / Textures at left. Small dimensional folders, Q scene-file icons Hallway / Courtyard, and a few gray material sphere thumbnails across the content well. These asset types should have varied familiar icon treatments like old creator tools, not one unified generic monochrome glyph language.
Slim functional status bar: "1 Mesh Selected".
Do not add Play, Blueprints, animation, timeline, a music player, new modes or extra app features.

OUTPUT / QUALITY:
One full-frame, front-on landscape desktop screenshot, approximately 16:9, high-resolution legible text. No outer presentation board. No giant branding or explanation on image. No dirt, grunge, punk typography, torn paper, gothic ornaments, physical rivets, music props, fluorescent neon, futuristic font or sci-fi chamfers. The distinctive quality must come from actual EARLY UE4-STYLE SHAPED CHROME, PICTORIAL ICONS, VARIED CONTROL FORMS AND CHARCOAL GRAY DEPTH, translated to Quader. Closely consult Images 1 and 2 instead of smoothing their character into modern uniformity.
